author: Chris Bloomstran
title: Semper Augustus 2025 Letter to Clients: Both Sides Now
headline: Chris Bloomstran after a 41.4% year: the S&P 500 sits on a “secular plateau”, and AI is a classic capital-cycle bubble apt to end badly.
summary: Semper Augustus returned 41.4% net in 2025 against 17.9% for the S&P 500, helped by dollar stores and gold miners; its stocks have earned 12.4% a year since 1999. Bloomstran argues that the cap-weighted US market has never been more concentrated or overvalued, at 26 times earnings on a near-record profit margin. He calls AI a classic capital-cycle bubble built on debt, circular financing and accounting gimmicks, with OpenAI valued at 65 times 2025 sales while burning at least $17 billion a year. His own portfolio trades at 12.2 times earnings. Berkshire, his largest holding, ended 2025 at 88% of his $1.23 trillion value estimate as Greg Abel takes over.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Bought Deckers Outdoor near its 2025 low after a 49% fall, and added to Five Below during the tariff sell-off.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Trimmed Kinross Gold heavily after a 204% rise to pay for other purchases.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Dollar General, Dollar Tree and Five Below grew from 17.1% to 25.9% of holdings during the year and drove much of the return.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: Berkshire trades at 88% of his intrinsic-value estimate of $570 per B share: about 14% upside plus annual growth in value.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: OpenAI is seeking $100 billion at an $830 billion valuation; Nvidia’s investments in it look to him like a gift card to buy more Nvidia chips.

risks.text: The cap-weighted US market has never been more concentrated or overvalued; perhaps 60 to 100 of the largest companies are priced to perfection.
Formerly capital-light tech giants are leveraging their balance sheets in an AI arms race, and their margins may come under pressure of their own making.
High prices combined with high profit margins usually mean mediocre future returns, or worse.

quotes.text: This one is apt to end badly.
